content.text:
This is a UI-only refactor: `LocationPicker` is extracted as a presentational component (React auto-escapes `c.name`/`c.country`), and `useLocationPicker` wraps existing browser APIs (`geocode.searchCities`, `geolocate.getCurrentPosition`, `permissionState`).

Data-flow check:
- `search(q)` → the existing `searchCities` already `encodeURIComponent`s the query; no injection sink is added.
- `useMyLocation()` → coordinates are handed to an in-app `onPick` callback; no new outbound sink. Errors set hardcoded copy (`DENIED_COPY`/`FAILED_COPY`), so no external error content or coordinates leak to logs/UI.
- `permissionState()` in effect only reads permission API state; cannot prompt.
- `weather-strip.tsx` change is a pure delegation to `LocationPicker`; same props flow through, no new sink.

No new entry points, no XSS/injection/SSRF/authz/traversal surface, no logging-of-secrets, no allowlist edit, no gate/action mismatch. The only observable non-security behaviors (no AbortController on `searchCities`, `onSearch` still firing per keystroke at the caller) are UX/correctness, not security defects introduced by this diff.
